historical_references.reference: Saint Laura, a virgin and martyr, was a native of the city of Thebes in Egypt. She was tortured and martyred during the Diocletian Persecution in the late 3rd century. According to legend, she was subjected to various forms of torment, including being burned at the stake, thrown into a pit of wild beasts, and having her limbs cut off. Despite her injuries, she remained steadfast in her faith and was eventually beheaded. She is now venerated as a saint in the Orthodox and Catholic Churches.

Laura of the Cave, also known as Laura Secunda or Laura of Thebes, was a 15th-century ascetic and mystic. She lived in a cave near the town of Santa Caterina in Italy and was known for her deep contemplative prayer and holiness. Her life was chronicled by St. Jerome, who visited her several times. She was particularly famous for her practice of the 'prayer of the heart,' which involved keeping the mind focused on God through repeated use of a holy word or name. Laura is now venerated as a saint in the Orthodox and Catholic Churches.
